units.leftText: Paul and Timothy, servants of Christ Jesus, To all the saints in Christ Jesus at Philippi, together with the overseers and deacons:
units.rightText: Paul and Timothy, servants of Christ Jesus, to all the saints in Christ Jesus that are at Philippi, with the bishops and deacons:

units.leftText: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. Thanksgiving and Prayer (1 Corinthians 1:4–9|1CO 1:4-9*; Colossians 1:3–14|COL 1:3-14*)
units.rightText: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

units.leftText: I thank my God every time I remember you.
units.rightText: I thank my God upon all my remembrance of you,

units.leftText: In every prayer for all of you, I always pray with joy,
units.rightText: always in every supplication of mine on behalf of you all making my supplication with joy,

units.leftText: because of your partnership in the gospel from the first day until now,
units.rightText: for your fellowship in furtherance of the gospel from the first day until now;

units.leftText: being confident of this, that He who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion until the day of Christ Jesus.
units.rightText: being confident of this very thing, that he who began a good work in you will perfect it until the day of Jesus Christ:

units.leftText: It is right for me to feel this way about all of you, since I have you in my heart. For in my chains and in my defense and confirmation of the gospel, you are all partners in grace with me.
units.rightText: even as it is right for me to be thus minded on behalf of you all, because I have you in my heart, inasmuch as, both in my bonds and in the defence and confirmation of the gospel, ye all are partakers with me of grace.

units.leftText: God is my witness how I long for all of you with the affection of Christ Jesus.
units.rightText: For God is my witness, how I long after you all in the tender mercies of Christ Jesus.

units.leftText: And this is my prayer: that your love may abound more and more in knowledge and depth of insight,
units.rightText: And this I pray, that your love may abound yet more and more in knowledge and all discernment;

units.leftText: so that you may be able to test and prove what is best and may be pure and blameless for the day of Christ,
units.rightText: so that ye may approve the things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere and void of offence unto the day of Christ;

units.leftText: filled with the fruit of righteousness that comes through Jesus Christ, to the glory and praise of God. Paul’s Trials Advance the Gospel (James 1:2–12|JAS 1:2-12*)
units.rightText: being filled with the fruits of righteousness, which are through Jesus Christ, unto the glory and praise of God.

units.leftText: Now I want you to know, brothers, that my circumstances have actually served to advance the gospel.
units.rightText: Now I would have you know, brethren, that the things which happened unto me have fallen out rather unto the progress of the gospel;

units.leftText: As a result, it has become clear throughout the whole palace guard and to everyone else that I am in chains for Christ.
units.rightText: so that my bonds became manifest in Christ throughout the whole prætorian guard, and to all the rest;

units.leftText: And most of the brothers, confident in the Lord by my chains, now dare more greatly to speak the word without fear.
units.rightText: and that most of the brethren in the Lord, being confident through my bonds, are more abundantly bold to speak the word of God without fear.
leftNotes: 1:14 NE and WH the word of God

units.leftText: It is true that some preach Christ out of envy and rivalry, but others out of goodwill.
units.rightText: Some indeed preach Christ even of envy and strife; and some also of good will:

units.leftText: The latter do so in love, knowing that I am appointed for the defense of the gospel.
units.rightText: the one do it of love, knowing that I am set for the defence of the gospel;
leftNotes: 1:16 BYZ and TR reverse the order of verses 16 and 17.

units.leftText: The former, however, preach Christ out of selfish ambition, not sincerely, supposing that they can add to the distress of my chains.
units.rightText: but the other proclaim Christ of faction, not sincerely, thinking to raise up affliction for me in my bonds.

units.leftText: What then is the issue? Just this: that in every way, whether by false motives or true, Christ is preached. And in this I rejoice. Yes, and I will continue to rejoice,
units.rightText: What then? only that in every way, whether in pretence or in truth, Christ is proclaimed; and therein I rejoice, yea, and will rejoice.

units.leftText: because I know that through your prayers and the provision of the Spirit of Jesus Christ, my distress will turn out for my deliverance.
units.rightText: For I know that this shall turn out to my salvation, through your supplication and the supply of the Spirit of Jesus Christ,

units.leftText: I eagerly expect and hope that I will in no way be ashamed, but will have complete boldness so that now as always Christ will be exalted in my body, whether by life or by death. To Live Is Christ
units.rightText: according to my earnest expectation and hope, that in nothing shall I be put to shame, but that with all boldness, as always, so now also Christ shall be magnified in my body, whether by life, or by death.

units.leftText: For to me, to live is Christ, and to die is gain.
units.rightText: For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain.

units.leftText: But if I go on living in the body, this will mean fruitful labor for me. So what shall I choose? I do not know.
units.rightText: But if to live in the flesh,— if this shall bring fruit from my work, then what I shall choose I know not.

units.leftText: I am torn between the two. I desire to depart and be with Christ, which is far better indeed.
units.rightText: But I am in a strait betwixt the two, having the desire to depart and be with Christ; for it is very far better:

units.leftText: But it is more necessary for you that I remain in the body.
units.rightText: yet to abide in the flesh is more needful for your sake.

units.leftText: Convinced of this, I know that I will remain and will continue with all of you for your progress and joy in the faith,
units.rightText: And having this confidence, I know that I shall abide, yea, and abide with you all, for your progress and joy in the faith;

units.leftText: so that through my coming to you again your exultation in Christ Jesus will resound on account of me. Worthy of the Gospel
units.rightText: that your glorying may abound in Christ Jesus in me through my presence with you again.

units.leftText: Nevertheless, conduct yourselves in a manner worthy of the gospel of Christ. Then, whether I come and see you or only hear about you in my absence, I will know that you stand firm in one spirit, contending together as one for the faith of the gospel,
units.rightText: Only let your manner of life be worthy of the gospel of Christ: that, whether I come and see you or be absent, I may hear of your state, that ye stand fast in one spirit, with one soul striving for the faith of the gospel;
leftNotes: 1:27 Or striving together with one mind

units.leftText: without being frightened in any way by those who oppose you. This is a clear sign of their destruction but of your salvation, and it is from God.
units.rightText: and in nothing affrighted by the adversaries: which is for them an evident token of perdition, but of your salvation, and that from God;

units.leftText: For it has been granted to you on behalf of Christ not only to believe in Him, but also to suffer for Him,
units.rightText: because to you it hath been granted in the behalf of Christ, not only to believe on him, but also to suffer in his behalf:

units.leftText: since you are encountering the same struggle you saw I had, and now hear that I still have.
units.rightText: having the same conflict which ye saw in me, and now hear to be in me.

units.leftText: Therefore if you have any encouragement in Christ, if any comfort from His love, if any fellowship with the Spirit, if any affection and compassion,
units.rightText: If there is therefore any exhortation in Christ, if any consolation of love, if any fellowship of the Spirit, if any tender mercies and compassions,

units.leftText: then make my joy complete by being like-minded, having the same love, being united in spirit and purpose.
units.rightText: make full my joy, that ye be of the same mind, having the same love, being of one accord, of one mind;

units.leftText: Do nothing out of selfish ambition or empty pride, but in humility consider others more important than yourselves.
units.rightText: doing nothing through faction or through vainglory, but in lowliness of mind each counting other better than himself;

units.leftText: Each of you should look not only to your own interests, but also to the interests of others. The Mind of Christ (Isaiah 52:13–15|ISA 52:13-15*)
units.rightText: not looking each of you to his own things, but each of you also to the things of others.

units.leftText: Let this mind be in you which was also in Christ Jesus:
units.rightText: Have this mind in you, which was also in Christ Jesus:

units.leftText: Who, existing in the form of God, did not consider equality with God something to be grasped,
units.rightText: who, existing in the form of God, counted not the being on an equality with God a thing to be grasped,

units.leftText: but emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in human likeness.
units.rightText: but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men;

units.leftText: And being found in appearance as a man, He humbled Himself and became obedient to death — even death on a cross.
units.rightText: and being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, becoming obedient even unto death, yea, the death of the cross.

units.leftText: Therefore God exalted Him to the highest place and gave Him the name above all names,
units.rightText: Wherefore also God highly exalted him, and gave unto him the name which is above every name;

units.leftText: that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, in heaven and on earth and under the earth,
units.rightText: that in the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven and things on earth and things under the earth,

units.leftText: and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father. Lights in the World (Matthew 5:13–16|MAT 5:13-16*)
units.rightText: and that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.

units.leftText: Therefore, my beloved, just as you have always obeyed, not only in my presence, but now even more in my absence, continue to work out your salvation with fear and trembling.
units.rightText: So then, my beloved, even as ye have always obeyed, not as in my presence only, but now much more in my absence, work out your own salvation with fear and trembling;

units.leftText: For it is God who works in you to will and to act on behalf of His good purpose.
units.rightText: for it is God who worketh in you both to will and to work, for his good pleasure.

units.leftText: Do everything without complaining or arguing,
units.rightText: Do all things without murmurings and questionings:

units.leftText: so that you may be blameless and pure, children of God without fault in a crooked and perverse generation, in which you shine as lights in the world
units.rightText: that ye may become blameless and harmless, children of God without blemish in the midst of a crooked and perverse generation, among whom ye are seen as lights in the world,

units.leftText: as you hold forth the word of life, in order that I may boast on the day of Christ that I did not run or labor in vain.
units.rightText: holding forth the word of life; that I may have whereof to glory in the day of Christ, that I did not run in vain neither labor in vain.

units.leftText: But even if I am being poured out like a drink offering on the sacrifice and service of your faith, I am glad and rejoice with all of you.
units.rightText: Yea, and if I am offered upon the sacrifice and service of your faith, I joy, and rejoice with you all:

units.leftText: So you too should be glad and rejoice with me. Timothy and Epaphroditus (1 Corinthians 16:10–12|1CO 16:10-12*)
units.rightText: and in the same manner do ye also joy, and rejoice with me.

units.leftText: Now I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you soon, that I also may be cheered when I learn how you are doing.
units.rightText: But I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy shortly unto you, that I also may be of good comfort, when I know your state.

units.leftText: I have nobody else like him who will genuinely care for your needs.
units.rightText: For I have no man likeminded, who will care truly for your state.

units.leftText: For all the others look after their own interests, not those of Jesus Christ.
units.rightText: For they all seek their own, not the things of Jesus Christ.

units.leftText: But you know Timothy’s proven worth, that as a child with his father he has served with me to advance the gospel.
units.rightText: But ye know the proof of him, that, as a child serveth a father, so he served with me in furtherance of the gospel.

units.leftText: So I hope to send him as soon as I see what happens with me.
units.rightText: Him therefore I hope to send forthwith, so soon as I shall see how it will go with me:

units.leftText: And I trust in the Lord that I myself will come soon.
units.rightText: but I trust in the Lord that I myself also shall come shortly.

units.leftText: But I thought it necessary to send back to you Epaphroditus, my brother, fellow worker, and fellow soldier, who is also your messenger and minister to my needs.
units.rightText: But I counted it necessary to send to you Epaphroditus, my brother and fellow-worker and fellow-soldier, and your messenger and minister to my need;

units.leftText: For he has been longing for all of you and is distressed because you heard he was ill.
units.rightText: since he longed after you all, and was sore troubled, because ye had heard that he was sick:

units.leftText: He was sick indeed, nearly unto death. But God had mercy on him, and not only on him but also on me, to spare me sorrow upon sorrow.
units.rightText: for indeed he was sick nigh unto death: but God had mercy on him; and not on him only, but on me also, that I might not have sorrow upon sorrow.

units.leftText: Therefore I am all the more eager to send him, so that when you see him again you may rejoice, and I may be less anxious.
units.rightText: I have sent him therefore the more diligently, that, when ye see him again, ye may rejoice, and that I may be the less sorrowful.

units.leftText: Welcome him in the Lord with great joy, and honor men like him,
units.rightText: Receive him therefore in the Lord with all joy; and hold such in honor:

units.leftText: because he nearly died for the work of Christ, risking his life to make up for your deficit of service to me.
units.rightText: because for the work of Christ he came nigh unto death, hazarding his life to supply that which was lacking in your service toward me.

units.leftText: Finally, my brothers, rejoice in the Lord. It is no trouble for me to write the same things to you again, and it is a safeguard for you.
units.rightText: Finally, my brethren, rejoice in the Lord. To write the same things to you, to me indeed is not irksome, but for you it is safe.

units.leftText: Watch out for those dogs, those workers of evil, those mutilators of the flesh!
units.rightText: Beware of the dogs, beware of the evil workers, beware of the concision:

units.leftText: For it is we who are the circumcision, we who worship by the Spirit of God, who glory in Christ Jesus, and who put no confidence in the flesh —
units.rightText: for we are the circumcision, who worship by the Spirit of God, and glory in Christ Jesus, and have no confidence in the flesh:

units.leftText: though I myself could have such confidence.
units.rightText: though I myself might have confidence even in the flesh: if any other man thinketh to have confidence in the flesh, I yet more:

units.leftText: circumcised on the eighth day, of the people of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin; a Hebrew of Hebrews; as to the law, a Pharisee;
units.rightText: circumcised the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews; as touching the law, a Pharisee;

units.leftText: as to zeal, persecuting the church; as to righteousness in the law, faultless.
units.rightText: as touching zeal, persecuting the church; as touching the righteousness which is in the law, found blameless.

units.leftText: But whatever was gain to me I count as loss for the sake of Christ.
units.rightText: Howbeit what things were gain to me, these have I counted loss for Christ.

units.leftText: More than that, I count all things as loss compared to the surpassing excellence of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord, for whom I have lost all things. I consider them rubbish, that I may gain Christ
units.rightText: Yea verily, and I count all things to be loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord: for whom I suffered the loss of all things, and do count them but refuse, that I may gain Christ,

units.leftText: and be found in Him, not having my own righteousness from the law, but that which is through faith in Christ, the righteousness from God on the basis of faith.
units.rightText: and be found in him, not having a righteousness of mine own, even that which is of the law, but that which is through faith in Christ, the righteousness which is from God by faith:
leftNotes: 3:9 Or through the faithfulness of Christ

units.leftText: I want to know Christ and the power of His resurrection and the fellowship of His sufferings, being conformed to Him in His death,
units.rightText: that I may know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, becoming conformed unto his death;

units.leftText: and so, somehow, to attain to the resurrection from the dead. Pressing on toward the Goal
units.rightText: if by any means I may attain unto the resurrection from the dead.

units.leftText: Not that I have already obtained all this, or have already been made perfect, but I press on to take hold of that for which Christ Jesus took hold of me.
units.rightText: Not that I have already obtained, or am already made perfect: but I press on, if so be that I may lay hold on that for which also I was laid hold on by Christ Jesus.

units.leftText: Brothers, I do not consider myself yet to have taken hold of it. But one thing I do: Forgetting what is behind and straining toward what is ahead,
units.rightText: Brethren, I count not myself yet to have laid hold: but one thing I do, forgetting the things which are behind, and stretching forward to the things which are before,

units.leftText: I press on toward the goal to win the prize of God’s heavenly calling in Christ Jesus.
units.rightText: I press on toward the goal unto the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.

units.leftText: All of us who are mature should embrace this point of view. And if you think differently about some issue, God will reveal this to you as well.
units.rightText: Let us therefore, as many as are perfect, be thus minded: and if in anything ye are otherwise minded, this also shall God reveal unto you:

units.leftText: Nevertheless, we must live up to what we have already attained. Citizenship in Heaven
units.rightText: only, whereunto we have attained, by that same rule let us walk.

units.leftText: Join one another in following my example, brothers, and carefully observe those who walk according to the pattern we set for you.
units.rightText: Brethren, be ye imitators together of me, and mark them that so walk even as ye have us for an ensample.

units.leftText: For as I have often told you before, and now say again even with tears: Many live as enemies of the cross of Christ.
units.rightText: For many walk, of whom I told you often, and now tell you even weeping, that they are the enemies of the cross of Christ:

units.leftText: Their end is destruction, their god is their belly, and their glory is in their shame. Their minds are set on earthly things.
units.rightText: whose end is perdition, whose god is the belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things.

units.leftText: But our citizenship is in heaven, and we eagerly await a Savior from there, the Lord Jesus Christ,
units.rightText: For our citizenship is in heaven; whence also we wait for a Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ:

units.leftText: who, by the power that enables Him to subject all things to Himself, will transform our lowly bodies to be like His glorious body.
units.rightText: who shall fashion anew the body of our humiliation, that it may be conformed to the body of his glory, according to the working whereby he is able even to subject all things unto himself.

units.leftText: Therefore, my brothers, whom I love and long for, my joy and crown, that is how you must stand firm in the Lord, my beloved.
units.rightText: Wherefore, my brethren beloved and longed for, my joy and crown, so stand fast in the Lord, my beloved.

units.leftText: I urge Euodia and Syntyche to agree with each other in the Lord.
units.rightText: I exhort Euodia, and I exhort Syntyche, to be of the same mind in the Lord.

units.leftText: Yes, and I ask you, my true yokefellow, to help these women who have contended at my side for the gospel, along with Clement and the rest of my fellow workers, whose names are in the Book of Life.
units.rightText: Yea, I beseech thee also, true yokefellow, help these women, for they labored with me in the gospel, with Clement also, and the rest of my fellow-workers, whose names are in the book of life.
leftNotes: 4:3 Or I ask you, loyal Syzygus

units.leftText: Rejoice in the Lord always. I will say it again: Rejoice!
units.rightText: Rejoice in the Lord always: again I will say, Rejoice.

units.leftText: Let your gentleness be apparent to all. The Lord is near.
units.rightText: Let your forbearance be known unto all men. The Lord is at hand.

units.leftText: Be anxious for nothing, but in everything, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God.
units.rightText: In nothing be anxious; but in everything by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God.

units.leftText: And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.
units.rightText: And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.

units.leftText: Finally, brothers, whatever is true, whatever is honorable, whatever is right, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, whatever is admirable — if anything is excellent or praiseworthy — think on these things.
units.rightText: Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honorable, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things.

units.leftText: Whatever you have learned or received or heard from me, or seen in me, put it into practice. And the God of peace will be with you. The Generosity of the Philippians (2 Corinthians 8:1–15|2CO 8:1-15*)
units.rightText: The things which ye both learned and received and heard and saw in me, these things do: and the God of peace shall be with you.

units.leftText: Now I rejoice greatly in the Lord that at last you have revived your concern for me. You were indeed concerned, but you had no opportunity to show it.
units.rightText: But I rejoice in the Lord greatly, that now at length ye have revived your thought for me; wherein ye did indeed take thought, but ye lacked opportunity.

units.leftText: I am not saying this out of need, for I have learned to be content regardless of my circumstances.
units.rightText: Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therein to be content.

units.leftText: I know how to live humbly, and I know how to abound. In any and every situation I have learned the secret of being filled and being hungry, of having plenty and having need.
units.rightText: I know how to be abased, and I know also how to abound: in everything and in all things have I learned the secret both to be filled and to be hungry, both to abound and to be in want.

units.leftText: I can do all things through Christ who gives me strength.
units.rightText: I can do all things in him that strengtheneth me.
leftNotes: 4:13 NA, SBL, NE, and WH in the One who gives me strength. BYZ and TR in Christ who gives me strength.

units.leftText: Nevertheless, you have done well to share in my affliction.
units.rightText: Howbeit ye did well that ye had fellowship with my affliction.

units.leftText: And as you Philippians know, in the early days of the gospel, when I left Macedonia, no church but you partnered with me in the matter of giving and receiving.
units.rightText: And ye yourselves also know, ye Philippians, that in the beginning of the gospel, when I departed from Macedonia, no church had fellowship with me in the matter of giving and receiving but ye only;

units.leftText: For even while I was in Thessalonica, you provided for my needs again and again.
units.rightText: for even in Thessalonica ye sent once and again unto my need.

units.leftText: Not that I am seeking a gift, but I am looking for the fruit that may be credited to your account.
units.rightText: Not that I seek for the gift; but I seek for the fruit that increaseth to your account.

units.leftText: I have all I need and more, now that I have received your gifts from Epaphroditus. They are a fragrant offering, an acceptable sacrifice, well-pleasing to God.
units.rightText: But I have all things, and abound: I am filled, having received from Epaphroditus the things that came from you, an odor of a sweet smell, a sacrifice acceptable, well-pleasing to God.

units.leftText: And my God will supply all your needs according to His glorious riches in Christ Jesus.
units.rightText: And my God shall supply every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus.

units.leftText: To our God and Father be glory forever and ever. Amen. Final Greetings (Ephesians 6:21–24|EPH 6:21-24*; 2 Timothy 4:19–22|2TI 4:19-22*)
units.rightText: Now unto our God and Father be the glory for ever and ever. Amen.

units.leftText: Greet all the saints in Christ Jesus. The brothers who are with me send you greetings.
units.rightText: Salute every saint in Christ Jesus. The brethren that are with me salute you.

units.leftText: All the saints send you greetings, especially those from the household of Caesar.
units.rightText: All the saints salute you, especially they that are of Cæsar’s household.

units.leftText: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.
units.rightText: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.
